question: Commissioner Wojciechowski spent 2023 for the most part campaigning on behalf of his party, PiS, for the elections in Poland, boasting about how much Union funding he had shifted to Poland for Polish agriculture, especially in favour of pig and poultry farmers. In the Commission’s view, are the public behaviour and statements of the Commissioner during the election campaign in Poland compatible with his duties, and what consequences does the Commission intend to draw from this conduct?
answer: The portfolio of the Commissioner for Agriculture naturally entails his participation in numerous meetings and events during which he is expected to explain the EU’s agricultural policy and its benefits.

In the context of the reply to this parliamentary question, the Commissioner has been consulted and clarified that he had not campaigned on behalf of his political party (Prawo i Sprawiedliwość, PiS) for the Polish elections held in 2023 and that his statements concerning EU funding for the Polish agricultural sector had been factual and had reflected the decisions taken by the European institutions.

According to Article 17(3) of the Treaty on European Union, the Members of the Commission shall be completely independent in carrying out their responsibilities. They neither seek nor take instructions from any government or other institution, body, office or entity.
The Commissioner for Agriculture, as all the other Members of the Commission, is committed to the respect of the obligations imposed on him by the Treaties.
